I farm for a living, and at my age I keep the plan steady, labor-saving, and reliable. I have 15.3 mu, well irrigation, and a wheat-maize system already suited to my land, so I will keep most of the land in wheat followed by maize because that gives me stable grain output and fits the way I have farmed for years. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I will avoid anything too complicated or too labor-intensive on the whole farm. I will leave a smaller part for cotton, because I already grow it and I want some cash income, but I will not expand it too much since cotton needs more field watching and more spraying. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen for steady tillering and grain filling, and irrigate at the key times because I have a well. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land, using no-tillage or very light tillage to save time and catch soil moisture. For cotton, I will keep inputs moderate but not low, especially potassium and pest control, because cotton suffers if I let it go. Overall, I will choose the safer path: stable grain area, limited cotton area, moderate fertilizer, and irrigation timed to protect yield.
